title: Exact abelian colimits over almost filtered categories
statement: Use the small-category universe convention of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $I$ be a small category with the following properties: (a) for every pair $a:w\to x$, $b:w\to y$ there exist $c:x\to z$, $d:y\to z$ such that $c\circ a=d\circ b$; (b) for every parallel pair $a,b:x\to y$ there exists $c:y\to z$ such that $c\circ a=c\circ b$. Neither nonemptiness nor connectedness is required. Let $\operatorname{Ab}$ denote the category of abelian groups in a universe containing the objects and arrows of $I$. All colimits [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] of diagrams $I\to\operatorname{Ab}$ exist. The colimit functor $\operatorname{colim}_I:\operatorname{Fun}(I,\operatorname{Ab})\to\operatorname{Ab}$ is additive and preserves finite limits. In particular, if $0\to F_1\to F_2\to F_3\to0$ is a sequence of diagrams whose evaluation at every $i\in I$ is a short exact sequence of abelian groups, then $0\to\operatorname{colim}_IF_1\to\operatorname{colim}_IF_2\to\operatorname{colim}_IF_3\to0$ is short exact. The empty index category is included: its colimit is the zero group.

source.place: Tag 04B0 (lemma-almost-directed-colimit-exact), with the two hypotheses of Categories Tag 002X (lemma-split-into-directed) expanded; additivity by the colimit universal property.

proof.text: For any small diagram $F:I\to\operatorname{Ab}$, form the group $S=\bigoplus_{i\in\operatorname{Ob}I}F(i)$ of finite-support tuples and its subgroup $R$ generated by $e_i(x)-e_k(F(a)x)$ for all $a:i\to k$ and $x\in F(i)$. The maps $x\mapsto[e_i(x)]$ to $S/R$ form a cocone. A cocone $h_i:F(i)\to T$ defines $S\to T$ by $(x_i)\mapsto\sum_i h_i(x_i)$; the cocone equations kill each generator of $R$, so it factors uniquely through $S/R$. Conversely any map from $S/R$ gives those component maps. This is exactly the colimit universal property of [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], and proves existence without any condition on $I$. All sums, generators and quotients lie in the chosen containing universe. For empty $I$, $S=R=0$ and the colimit is $0$.

source.place: Tag 00D5 (lemma-colimit), quotient construction and universal-property proof, with the same relations indexed by all arrows rather than a preorder; used in Tag 04B0.

proof.text: For natural transformations $u,v:F\to G$, the induced maps on colimits satisfy $(\operatorname{colim}(u+v))\iota_i=\iota_i^G(u_i+v_i)=((\operatorname{colim}u)+(\operatorname{colim}v))\iota_i$. The uniqueness clause of [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] makes the two maps equal. The same calculation gives preservation of zero morphisms. Thus the colimit functor is additive.

source.place: Tag 04B0, additivity supplement from the colimit universal property.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-almost-filtered-components] to precisely hypotheses (a) and (b). Obtain a small set $J$ and nonempty filtered full subcategories $I_j$, partitioning the objects, with no arrows between different parts. Their objects and arrows remain small. If $I$ is empty, $J$ is empty; filteredness is asserted only for the nonempty parts.

source.place: Tag 04B0 (lemma-almost-directed-colimit-exact), first sentence of proof, invoking Categories Tag 002X (lemma-split-into-directed).

proof.text: Put $C_j(F)=\operatorname{colim}_{I_j}F|_{I_j}$. Then $\operatorname{colim}_I F\cong\bigoplus_{j\in J}C_j(F)$. Indeed, a cocone $F\to T$ is exactly one cocone $F|_{I_j}\to T$ for each $j$, since every arrow stays in its part. By [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] these are exactly homomorphisms $C_j(F)\to T$, and they assemble uniquely by finite summation to a homomorphism from the direct sum. The comparison sends every $F(i)$, $i\in I_j$, through its own summand. A natural transformation induces the direct sum of its component-colimit maps, as follows by testing on these coprojections. Thus this identification respects every map of diagrams, including the maps of exact sequences and finite limit diagrams.

source.place: Tag 04B0, reduction from the disjoint filtered components to their coproduct, expanded by universal properties.

proof.text: On each $I_j$, [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimits-commute-finite-limits] applies to abelian-group diagrams, since $I_j$ is small and nonempty filtered. In particular $C_j$ preserves the zero group, binary products and equalizers. These limits in $\operatorname{Fun}(I,\operatorname{Ab})$ are pointwise: form the indicated groups at each object, with transition maps induced by those of the diagram. A cone factors uniquely objectwise, and uniqueness makes these factors natural. Restricting these pointwise constructions to $I_j$ therefore gives exactly the limits to which the cited comparison applies.

source.place: Tag 04B0, filtered-component argument; Categories Tag 002W (lemma-directed-commutes), abelian-group finite-limit comparison.

proof.text: Direct sums commute with the three preceding constructions by finite support. First $\bigoplus_j0=0$. Next $(\bigoplus_j A_j)\times(\bigoplus_j B_j)\cong\bigoplus_j(A_j\times B_j)$: pair the coordinates, using the union of the two finite supports; the inverse projects each coordinate. For maps $f_j,g_j:A_j\rightrightarrows B_j$, a tuple $(a_j)$ lies in the equalizer of $\bigoplus f_j,\bigoplus g_j$ exactly when $f_j(a_j)=g_j(a_j)$ for every $j$, so that equalizer is $\bigoplus_j\operatorname{Eq}(f_j,g_j)$. Together with steps 4 and 5 this proves preservation of zero, products and equalizers. For any finite diagram, its limit is the subgroup of the finite product of its object groups cut out by the equalities for each arrow; equivalently it is the equalizer of the two maps from that product to the product of the target groups over arrows. Hence preservation of the preceding three constructions proves preservation of every finite limit. The empty diagram gives $0$ on both sides.

source.place: Tag 04B0, last sentence: direct sums checked by hand, including empty families; finite-support verification of the finite-limit clause.

proof.text: For the given pointwise short exact sequence, restrict to $I_j$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-abelian-groups-exact] at each of its three nonzero positions, with zeros at the ends; component colimits of the zero diagram are zero by step 5. Thus $0\to C_j(F_1)\to C_j(F_2)\to C_j(F_3)\to0$ is short exact. Direct sums preserve this exactness explicitly: the first map is injective coordinate by coordinate; a middle tuple in the kernel has finitely many nonzero coordinates, and exactness supplies preimages at just those coordinates; a target tuple similarly has a preimage supported on its finite support. The direct sum of these sequences is therefore short exact. Step 4 identifies its maps with the required maps of colimits. With $J=\varnothing$ the sequence consists entirely of zero groups.

source.place: Tag 04B0, component exactness from Tag 00DB (lemma-directed-colimit-exact) and the final direct-sum exactness argument.

proof_origin.place: Tag 04B0 (lemma-almost-directed-colimit-exact), with the universal-property and finite-support arguments written out; finite-limit clause uses Categories Tag 002W.

lean.statement: theorem almostFiltered_abelian_colimits_exact (I : Type u) [SmallCategory I] (hspan : ∀ {v x y : I} (a : v ⟶ x) (b : v ⟶ y), ∃ (z : I) (c : x ⟶ z) (d : y ⟶ z), a ≫ c = b ≫ d) (hparallel : ∀ {x y : I} (a b : x ⟶ y), ∃ (z : I) (c : y ⟶ z), a ≫ c = b ≫ c) : HasColimitsOfShape I AddCommGrpCat.{max u w} ∧ (colim (J := I) (C := AddCommGrpCat.{max u w})).Additive ∧ PreservesFiniteLimits (colim (J := I) (C := AddCommGrpCat.{max u w})) ∧ (∀ S : ShortComplex (I ⥤ AddCommGrpCat.{max u w}), (∀ i : I, (S.map ((evaluation I AddCommGrpCat.{max u w}).obj i)).ShortExact) → (S.map (colim (J := I) (C := AddCommGrpCat.{max u w}))).ShortExact) ∧ (IsEmpty I → ∀ F : I ⥤ AddCommGrpCat.{max u w}, IsZero (colimit F))
